explanation.question_quote: pericardial calcifications and small tubular-shaped ventricles
explanation.sentence: Ultrasound shows pericardial calcification and small, tubular ventricles.
The jugular venous pressure fails to fall on inspiration (Kussmaul’s sign), a characteristic finding in constrictive pericarditis.
The prominent y descent reflects rapid early ventricular filling that stops abruptly when the rigid pericardium limits further expansion.
Chronic constrictive pericarditis best explains the findings because a scarred, calcified pericardium restricts diastolic filling and causes heart failure.
